title: Lena and the Wreck
premise: Hazel Kavanagh, a storm chaser drowning in debt to the Meridian Syndicate, accepts a dying prospector's map in exchange for a promise to deliver his findings to his estranged daughter. The map leads to the Wreck, a downed survey plane holding ore samples that could invalidate the Syndicate's fraudulent concession claims. Pursued by Syndicate enforcers and racing the first snows across the Carrow Range, Hazel must choose between selling the samples to clear her debt and honoring her promise. She delivers them, exposes the fraud through the daughter's testimony, and walks away still poor but finally free.
about_author: Quentin Zhou is the pen name of a former geologist who spent a decade mapping remote concession territory before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose promises outlast their prospects.

chapters.title: The Weight of Optimists
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Chasing a storm for hire money, she totals her truck and faces the Meridian Syndicate's collectors, who offer a brutal deadline. Emotional beat: desperation masked as bravado as she realizes her skills are worth more to predators than to herself.

chapters.title: A Dying Man's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Prospector Elias Wren, injured in a ravine, trades her a weathered map for a promise: deliver his case to his daughter Mara in Coldbrook. He dies at dusk. Emotional beat: reluctant oath-taking; Hazel accepts not from kindness but because the map might be worth something.

chapters.title: What the Map Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with an interlude of Syndicate enforcer Dade Rusk receiving orders. Studying the map, she recognizes the Wreck site inside Syndicate concession land. Emotional beat: dawning understanding that the promise has made her a target.

chapters.title: Coldbrook
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Hazel finds Mara Wren, who wants nothing of her father's legacy or his lies. She refuses the case. Emotional beat: rejection and shame; Hazel leaves with the case, now carrying two burdens instead of one.

chapters.title: The Concession Papers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In a border-town archive she discovers the ore samples could prove the Syndicate falsified assay data to win permits expiring at first snow. Emotional beat: the shift from fugitive to believer — justice suddenly has a shape she can hold.

chapters.title: Rusk on the Road
chapters.summary: Alternating Hazel and Rusk POVs. The enforcers corner her at a river crossing; she escapes by flooding the ford, losing most of her gear. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; she stops running toward escape and starts running toward the range.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Alone above the treeline, storm-reading skills become survival skills as early snows close in. A near-fatal fall costs her the compass Elias gave her. Emotional beat: stripped bare, she confronts why she keeps promises no one enforces.

chapters.title: The Wreck
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She reaches the plane, retrieves the sample case, and finds evidence Elias was the honest surveyor the Syndicate buried. Rusk arrives; a standoff in the fuselage ends with Rusk falling into the crevasse field. Emotional beat: triumph curdled by cost — she holds the truth and hates what it took.

chapters.title: Descent into Coldbrook
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Frostbitten, Hazel arrives as the snows seal the pass and gives Mara the case and her father's confession letter. Mara, moved by what Hazel endured rather than what Elias wrote, agrees to testify. Emotional beat: forgiveness arriving sideways, through action instead of words.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Permits voided, Syndicate officers indicted, Hazel declines a reward and buys back a battered truck instead. Mara sees her off. Emotional beat: quiet resolution — the debt to dangerous optimists remains unpaid, but Hazel has learned which debts define her.
